texts: Coronary ligation for ALCAPA is associated with a 25 percent late mortality: A.
Tying off the anomalous artery stops the steal but leaves a one-coronary circulation dependent on collaterals, with late infarction and sudden death.

Repairs that establish a two-coronary system, such as direct transfer or the Takeuchi operation, give far better results: most patients recover normal ventricular function, and mitral regurgitation usually improves without early valve surgery.
In the picture, one of the four tied-off hotels lies in a coffin later, while the hotels whose spike was moved stand well.
Memory hook: tie off Capone's spike, and one hotel in four is lost.
